topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks welcome the students and set out the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies, systemic toxicity, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional cancer treatment modalities, including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe strategies for targeting cancer-specific cellular vulnerabilities, including hormone dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted kinase inhibition, exploring oncogene addiction, drug mechanisms of action, and resistance pathways such as gatekeeper mutations and pathway bypass.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the use of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to specifically bind tumor antigens and deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer immunology and cellular immunotherapies, including immune surveillance, immune checkpoint inhibition, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Historical progress, therapeutic challenges, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of cancer therapy, reviewing historical mortality trends, clinical trial dilemmas, and future paradigms such as early detection and biomarker-driven care.
